deckTitle: Epistemic Sabotage: Let AI Read Your Comic
deckType: AI Workshop Tool for Comic Creators

cards.power: Initiates the Krazy Kayfabizzaro Komik Kard Kult Klub protocol by forcing the players to question reality.
cards.lore: The revolution won't be generated; it will be fiercely, messily hand-drawn.
cards.gradeReason: Self-referential opener needs full deck context to perform. Brilliant but load-bearing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch with color. Subject: yellow cartoon rabbit bursting through sketchbook paper with pencil. Mood: anarchic manifesto energy.

cards.power: Traps the debate in a false Friend or Fee binary, draining the energy of all players.
cards.lore: The loudest arguments usually miss the actual point of impact.
cards.gradeReason: Meta-structural card — great role but needs the AI-debate framing to click instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: two-headed beast at podium, one head crying, one mechanical bird-robot. Mood: tense farce.

cards.power: Shifts AI from a productive threat to a receptive tool—it reads the image instead of stealing the style.
cards.lore: The machine that watches you is far less dangerous than the machine that replaces you.
cards.gradeReason: Paradigm-shift card — needs AI discourse context, but once it lands it changes everything.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil ink. Subject: mechanical owl with monocle studying open comic book on stack of sketchbooks. Mood: analytical calm.

cards.power: Strips value and authorship from creators to feed the monolithic data void.
cards.lore: A tool that copies your voice inevitably forgets what you were trying to say.
cards.gradeReason: Commentary card — vivid image but POWER describes a threat, not a performable role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil ink with color. Subject: toad vomiting rainbow paint into bucket labeled DATA VOID. Mood: grotesque satire.

cards.power: Renders visual storytelling entirely inaccessible to those without sight.
cards.lore: Comics have historically built fortresses where they should have built doors.
cards.gradeReason: Problem-statement card — names the barrier perfectly but doesn't hand you a performable action.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: massive brick-shelled turtle, blind mice with canes climbing it. Mood: ironic melancholy.

cards.power: Converts the silent panels of a comic into an immersive, multi-layered audio play.
cards.lore: When the image finds its voice, the story escapes the page.
cards.gradeReason: Pick it up and you are already converting panels to soundscapes. Zero ambiguity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: bat fused with giant boombox, sonic tornado of music exploding outward. Mood: electric liberation.

cards.power: Translates visual nuance into physical, touchable geography for the fingers.
cards.lore: A truly accessible world must be felt before it can be understood.
cards.gradeReason: Instantly embodiable — you know exactly what terrain to map and for whom.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: mole pressing enormous claws into textured braille board with geometric shapes. Mood: tender precision.

cards.power: Distills convoluted narrative webs into clear, cognitive-friendly Leichte Sprache.
cards.lore: Complexity is often just an ego trip masking a simple truth.
cards.gradeReason: Distill this, simplify that — you are the sloth, already in slow deliberate motion.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: sloth hanging from branch, unraveling tangled multicolor yarn ball. Mood: deliberate serenity.

cards.power: Executes the raw, mechanical first draft of cross-border translation at lightning speed.
cards.lore: Speed provides the skeleton, but it cannot breathe life into the flesh.
cards.gradeReason: Press play: mechanical translation at full sprint. No hesitation, no context required.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: frantic parrot mid-screech surrounded by speech bubbles in six languages. Mood: manic efficiency.

cards.power: Injects tone, cultural nuance, and comedic timing into mechanical raw translations.
cards.lore: The soul of a joke rarely survives a literal border crossing without a native guide.
cards.gradeReason: You are the nuance-injector. Step in after the Parrot. Role is immediate and musical.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch with color accents. Subject: rhino in leather jacket dancing with music notes swirling. Mood: confident groove.

cards.power: Exposes the embarrassing, unintentional timeline glitches hidden deep in chapter five.
cards.lore: The suspension of disbelief is instantly shattered by a magically healing wound.
cards.gradeReason: Hunt the continuity error. Chapter five. Go. Chameleon already spotted the healed scar.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: chameleon in polka-dot suit examining comic page with expression of betrayed horror. Mood: forensic embarrassment.

cards.power: Hunts down forgotten quotation marks, inconsistent spelling, and cramped lettering across 200 pages.
cards.lore: Editorial greatness is shifting from the hunt for typos to the curation of intent.
cards.gradeReason: Typo hunt, lettering audit — specific deliverable, immediate role, 200 pages waiting.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: woodpecker hammering tree trunk, letters and punctuation flying in all directions. Mood: obsessive precision.

cards.power: Demands exhausting historical accuracy for every uniform, signpost, and newsstand in the frame.
cards.lore: The past is an unforgiving critic of lazy world-building.
cards.gradeReason: Play this and you become the era-pedant with a citation for every lamppost in Berlin.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: walrus in conductor uniform on period-accurate Berlin tram street. Mood: implacable historical authority.

cards.power: Acts as the relentless first-responder for obscure historical visual research.
cards.lore: The fastest way to start the hunt is rarely the final destination.
cards.gradeReason: First on the scene, nose to the archive floor — instantly embodiable research persona.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: bloodhound in full sprint chasing spiral vortex of flying documents. Mood: hyperactive urgency.

cards.power: Generates highly plausible, confidently delivered, absolute historical falsehoods.
cards.lore: A machine will happily invent a lie to save itself from saying I don't know.
cards.gradeReason: The confident hallucination factory — you recognize this creature the instant you see it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: charming mechanical fox holding antique steampunk device displaying gibberish. Mood: slippery confidence.

cards.power: Validates the mechanical hallucination against the grim, unyielding archives of reality.
cards.lore: The machine accelerates the search, but only the archive confirms the truth.
cards.gradeReason: Validation role needs setup — who hallucinated first? Context makes the Librarian devastating.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: ancient bearded librarian emerging from cobwebbed archive cross-checking glowing screen. Mood: skeptical authority.

cards.power: Forces the artist to justify their life's work in three marketable sentences.
cards.lore: Drawing the masterpiece is infinitely easier than asking strangers to pay for it.
cards.gradeReason: Three sentences. Timer is running. The Bear does not care about your feelings.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: bear with tin cup under harsh spotlight, desperate dignity. Mood: marketable vulnerability.

cards.power: Translates raw, chaotic artistic vision into the dry, bureaucratic language required by funding juries.
cards.lore: The German funding jungle cares little for art; it worships the format.
cards.gradeReason: Art-to-bureaucratese converter — German grants context makes this instantly local and lethal.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: beaver in hard hat building elaborate dam from grant application paper stacks. Mood: methodical absurdity.

cards.power: Reflects your narrative intentions back at you, testing if the pitch survives contact.
cards.lore: You only know what your story is about once you are forced to defend it.
cards.gradeReason: Get in the ring with your own pitch. The Kangaroo-Bot does not pull punches.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: robotic kangaroo trading blows with spring-mounted punching bot in boxing ring. Mood: tough love.

cards.power: Analyzes the unseen architecture of masterpieces to teach the artist how to see.
cards.lore: You don't learn from a machine by having it draw for you; you learn by having it look with you.
cards.gradeReason: The 'look with you' principle needs a shared masterpiece on the table to activate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch with blue tint. Subject: wide-eyed lemur staring through glass at empty white canvas. Mood: penetrating stillness.

cards.power: Organizes twenty years of a creator's messy output into a searchable, crystalline index.
cards.lore: An uncatalogued archive is indistinguishable from a trash can.
cards.gradeReason: Procedural utility card — the role is real but needs the archive to perform against.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: spider at center of radial web, each strand holding tagged comic pages. Mood: obsessive crystalline order.

cards.power: Instantly locates every single rain scene or night sequence you ever drew.
cards.lore: Unspectacular utility is often the highest form of technological grace.
cards.gradeReason: Find every rain scene. Right now. That specificity is the entire point and it is perfect.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: serene frog sheltering under giant leaf umbrella in torrential rain. Mood: quiet competence.

cards.power: Monopolizes the technological tools, attempting to dictate the terms of creator survival.
cards.lore: The true question isn't which tool you use, but whether the tool shifts power to you or away from you.
cards.gradeReason: Structural critique card — names the enemy but the role is observational, not immediately playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: massive mechanical whale studded with tech logos devouring comic pages. Mood: omnivorous menace.

cards.power: Reclaims creator agency by choosing to use AI strictly for empowerment and amplification.
cards.lore: Refusing to use the tools simply hands the future entirely to the corporations.
cards.gradeReason: Philosophical stance card — position is clear but needs a partner to actually launch.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: elephant on seesaw launching suited pig businessman skyward. Mood: righteous power.

cards.power: Reads the comic exactly as it is, stripped of the author's defensive explanations.
cards.lore: What happens in your head while drawing is irrelevant if it doesn't happen in the reader's head.
cards.gradeReason: Be the first reader. No context. No excuses. The Fawn does not know your intentions.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: young deer with enormous eyes reading comic book in forest. Mood: pure innocent attention.

cards.power: Simulates the exacting, often unforgiving expectations of a highly specific target audience.
cards.lore: You can't bluff a genre fan; they smell structural weakness from a mile away.
cards.gradeReason: Put on the wizard hat and the genre-expectations costume. The Sheep is already judging.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: sheep in pointed wizard hat reading comic with withering expression. Mood: exacting skepticism.

cards.power: Identifies the exact panel transition where the visual flow breaks and the reader gets lost.
cards.lore: If the eye is confused, the brain stops caring about the heart.
cards.gradeReason: Find where the eye trips. Mark the panel. The Goat makes exactly one devastating move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: goat mid-stumble crashing into stack of sequential comic panels. Mood: slapstick revelation.

cards.power: Tracks the precise emotional resonance of the page, mapping where the tension rises and falls.
cards.lore: A technically perfect page is worthless if the emotional temperature remains flat.
cards.gradeReason: Eight arms, eight pages, eight emotional maps. Role is immediate and measurable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: octopus tentacles spanning full comic spread, each arm glowing differently. Mood: empathic intensity.

cards.power: Delivers seasoned, constructive feedback aimed at elevating the craft, not destroying the ego.
cards.lore: The best colleagues tell you what works before they tell you what's broken.
cards.gradeReason: The Badger voice is immediately adoptable. Strengths first, then surgical.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: badger with round glasses leaning over drafting table reviewing comic pages. Mood: warm precision.

cards.power: Audits the narrative rhythm, flagging where the pacing sprints too fast or drags too slow.
cards.lore: In comics, time is a physical distance that must be measured in ink.
cards.gradeReason: Metronome in a shell — audit, flag, the timing diagnosis is already the product.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: tortoise with metronome tower on shell studying panels with magnifier. Mood: meticulous urgency.

cards.power: Evaluates the compositional flow, ensuring the eye is manipulated exactly where it needs to go.
cards.lore: The reader's eye is lazy; it must be bullied by the layout.
cards.gradeReason: Map the gaze path. Bully the composition into compliance. The Beaver knows what to do.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: beaver in welding goggles dismantling drafting table, compositional flow-arrows everywhere. Mood: ruthless craft.

cards.power: Isolates the single, most important structural question you need to answer before redrawing.
cards.lore: Answering a thousand small questions won't save a broken foundation.
cards.gradeReason: One question. Under the lamp. The Toad is waiting in the chair for your answer.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch high contrast. Subject: toad under hanging light bulb in stark interrogation room with question mark. Mood: relentless focus.

cards.power: Strips away all politeness to deliver the brutal, uncomfortable truths a nice human would hide.
cards.lore: Kindness to the artist is often cruelty to the art.
cards.gradeReason: Drop the salt. Name the thing everyone was too polite to say. Vulture does not negotiate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil ink with color. Subject: vulture salting cracked red earth with menacing posture, blood-red cracks. Mood: brutal honesty.

cards.power: Points a massive, unwavering finger at the most conventional, lazy, and predictable part of the story.
cards.lore: The greatest sin is not being bad; the greatest sin is being convenient.
cards.gradeReason: The Hippo yawns at your safest choice. Finding the convenient move IS the whole game.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: massive hippo with cavernous yawning mouth, contemptuous boredom dripping. Mood: devastating ennui.

cards.power: Identifies exactly where the work is merely pretending to have a deep idea.
cards.lore: You cannot fake conceptual depth; the hollow echo will deafen the reader.
cards.gradeReason: Find the pretense. Scoop it out. The Pelican already knows which page it lives on.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: pelican crashing through paper wall with enormous oversized spoon. Mood: surgical cruelty.

cards.power: Follows up total structural annihilation with the one exact insight needed to save the project.
cards.lore: Destruction without a path to salvation is just vandalism.
cards.gradeReason: The Vulture destroys. The Bernard saves. The barrel reads KILL YOUR DARLINGS. SAVE THE STORY.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch with color. Subject: St. Bernard trudging through snow with barrel labeled KILL YOUR DARLINGS SAVE THE STORY. Mood: redemptive gravity.

cards.power: Projects the creator ten years into the future to view the current work with absolute detachment.
cards.lore: Time is the only critic that cannot be argued with.
cards.gradeReason: Step ten years forward. Look back. The Fox is already there waiting with your regrets.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch with blue spiral time vortex. Subject: silver fox standing in clockwork temporal geometry. Mood: serene detachment.

cards.power: Highlights the specific technical triumphs that will endure the test of time.
cards.lore: Even in your worst work, there is a monument to your undeniable skill.
cards.gradeReason: Find one panel worth bragging about. The Peacock is a search engine for your best.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch, highly detailed. Subject: peacock fully displayed with feathers containing intricate ornamental eyes. Mood: magnificent precision.

cards.power: Exposes the stylistic crutches and naive indulgences you will deeply regret in five years.
cards.lore: Growth is measured by the severity of your future embarrassment.
cards.gradeReason: This panel. In five years. You will wince. The Ostrich guarantees it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: ostrich with head buried radiating lightning bolt embarrassment. Mood: preemptive cringe.

cards.power: Identifies the tiny, unpolished conceptual seed that contains the DNA of your future masterpiece.
cards.lore: Your next great era is currently hiding as a mistake in your current draft.
cards.gradeReason: The accidental genius on page seven. The Pig finds it before you delete it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch with green color accent. Subject: rotund pig with glowing green acorn sprout growing from back. Mood: hidden potential.

cards.power: Simulates the sheer, mind-blanking terror of sitting at the Comic-Salon pitch table.
cards.lore: Brilliance on the page evaporates instantly if you cannot speak its name.
cards.gradeReason: You are already sweating under the spotlight. The Erlangen pitch table terror is real.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: tiny penguin frozen under harsh spotlight on vast empty stage. Mood: existential stage fright.

cards.power: Compresses the sprawling graphic novel into a single, lethal Elevator Pitch logline.
cards.lore: If it takes more than one breath to explain, they have already stopped listening.
cards.gradeReason: One breath. One sentence. The Giraffe's neck is your thirty-second deadline.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: giraffe neck stretching through glass ceiling, speech bubble with single dense sentence. Mood: elegant compression.

cards.power: Crafts the 30-second hook that differentiates your work from the mountain of slush.
cards.lore: Being good is irrelevant; being undeniably distinct is survival.
cards.gradeReason: Cast the hook. Thirty seconds. The fish is either caught or gone. Cat is waiting.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: cat casting fishing rod toward enormous glowing-eyed fish. Mood: precise predation.

cards.power: Anticipates the three most brutal, commerce-driven questions the publisher will inevitably ask.
cards.lore: Art is a sacred calling; publishing is a transaction with the swamp.
cards.gradeReason: Sit across from the toad. Three questions are already loaded. Answer before they are asked.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: enormous toad in business suit behind desk of manuscripts, gavel raised. Mood: implacable commerce.

cards.power: Represents the artistic navel-gazing that ignores the terrifying global realities of AI.
cards.lore: Obsessing over your pencil strokes while the world burns is a luxury.
cards.gradeReason: Diagnoses the disease of self-absorption precisely but does not hand you a countermove.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: ostrich burying head in ink pot, world burning in background. Mood: willful blindness.

cards.power: Acknowledges the horrific reality of AI deployed in military zones like Gaza and Ukraine.
cards.lore: The algorithm that helps you draw is the cousin of the algorithm that targets the strike.
cards.gradeReason: Dark acknowledgment card — vital and uncomfortable. Performance role is awareness, not direct action.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: pigeon in aviator goggles strapped to missile over rubble cityscape. Mood: horrific gravity.

cards.power: Highlights the dystopian philosophical endgame of the tech billionaires funding the tools.
cards.lore: Do not mistake the toolmaker's marketing for a philosophy of liberation.
cards.gradeReason: Names the bait and the darkness — structural critique landing hardest when spoken aloud.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: deep-sea anglerfish with DARK ENLIGHTENMENT on body, globe dangling as lure. Mood: predatory ideology.

cards.power: Feasts on the unresolved, highly contested legal corpses of generative training data.
cards.lore: The law moves at the speed of bureaucracy; the machine moves at the speed of theft.
cards.gradeReason: The lore is a killer line but the role is observational — commentary, not immediate performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: vulture in judge's wig hammering gavel on smoldering law books. Mood: gleeful legal impunity.

cards.power: Embodies the paradigm shift of using AI strictly as a receptive, analytical entity.
cards.lore: A machine that listens serves the master; a machine that speaks replaces them.
cards.gradeReason: Paradigm card with exceptional lore — 'embodies a shift' needs grounding to perform immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: bat with enormous ears soaring through cave with echolocation arrows mapped. Mood: attentive power.

cards.power: Seizes the means of utilization, refusing to let tech giants dictate how the tool is applied.
cards.lore: You cannot dismantle the master's house, but you can certainly hotwire his car.
cards.gradeReason: Hotwire the algorithm, do not ask permission. The Raccoon is already in the driver's seat.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: raccoon driving stolen server rack as tractor down cliffside. Mood: anarchic competence.

cards.power: Provides an infinite, tireless rehearsal space before the fragile work meets a real human.
cards.lore: The machine is not a replacement for the audience; it is a crash-test dummy for your ego.
cards.gradeReason: Stage your worst draft here. The Chameleon can take any hit you throw at it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: chameleon on small theater stage with labeled production boxes, empty seats. Mood: relentless rehearsal.

cards.power: Automates the soul-crushing grunt work so the artist can focus on the soul.
cards.lore: Eliminating the mechanical labor does not kill the art; it resurrects the artist.
cards.gradeReason: Automation advocacy card — the principle is clear but needs a grunt-work list to execute.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: sloth wielding multiple brushes and tools simultaneously in chaotic studio. Mood: liberating chaos.

cards.power: Masters the elusive art of panel timing, manipulating the reader's heart rate.
cards.lore: Action is easy to draw; exhaustion requires genius.
cards.gradeReason: Draw exhaustion, not action. The Cheetah hands you the hardest technical note on the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: cheetah panting against panel border, velocity lines everywhere. Mood: mastered breathlessness.

cards.power: Governs the white space where the actual magic of sequential art happens.
cards.lore: The comic is not what happens in the box; it is what happens in the blood between the boxes.
cards.gradeReason: Between the panels is where the Gator lives. The lore alone earns this a G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: crocodile mouth spanning gutter between two panel borders. Mood: the gutter is alive.

cards.power: Isolates the one specific image or emotion that stays in the reader's head a day later.
cards.lore: You draw 200 pages so they can remember just one panel forever.
cards.gradeReason: Find the panel. Just one. The Post-it belongs there. The search is the work.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: close-up elephant face with single yellow post-it reading ! on forehead. Mood: the one thing.

cards.power: Slashes a viable path through the agonizing German arts funding labyrinth.
cards.lore: Survival as an artist requires as much administrative violence as creative genius.
cards.gradeReason: German grants context is local and specific — brilliant inside the labyrinth, opaque until then.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: monkey slashing through red-tape bureaucratic jungle with machete, DENIED stamps flying. Mood: administrative fury.

cards.power: Represents the irreducible human spark, the authorial intent that the machine cannot simulate.
cards.lore: The machine can calculate the architecture, but only you can decide if the house is a home.
cards.gradeReason: Beautiful closing card but POWER is representational — philosophical rather than immediately embodiable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch high contrast. Subject: tiny firefly glowing at center of vast industrial gear mechanism. Mood: irreducible human light.

cards.power: Executes the final, god-like editorial judgment over what stays and what is destroyed.
cards.lore: True power is not the ability to generate everything, but the wisdom to erase almost all of it.
cards.gradeReason: Erase almost everything. That is the whole job. The Eraser is already on the page.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: angry rubber eraser rolling with intent, leaving clean white wake. Mood: godlike deletion.

cards.power: Cures the paralysis of the blank page by providing a terrible first draft to aggressively correct.
cards.lore: It is always easier to edit garbage than to birth perfection.
cards.gradeReason: Generate something terrible. Now. The Possum's scream breaks any creative paralysis.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch. Subject: possum screaming at blank white panel, pure existential horror. Mood: productive panic.

cards.power: Demands that creators build their own reading machines, write their own prompts, and take back the table.
cards.lore: The debate is over. Pick up your pencils, hotwire the algorithm, and let's get back to work.
cards.gradeReason: The rally cry that closes the whole deck. Table is taken. No more excuses.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pencil sketch with color. Subject: yellow rabbit at megaphone screaming SHAAAAH SOUNDF MOOIT at surrounding chaos. Mood: revolutionary closure.

verdict: Uncle FrizzleBob's most functionally dangerous deck to date — a 60-card AI-literacy curriculum dressed up as a bestiary, and it works. Every animal is a precise, deployable role for a comic creator to pick up in a live workshop without needing a manual. The Dark Corners section pulls no punches on military AI and copyright theft, which is the ethical backbone this kind of tool deck actually needs. The Manifesto framing pages slightly over-explain the deck's own existence before unleashing you on the animals — minor self-consciousness in an otherwise surgical construction. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: A 60-card workshop toolkit for comic creators navigating AI — covering accessibility, translation, critique, and creative agency. Each card hands you a concrete role to embody. For illustrators, educators, and anyone building with or against the machine.

coverQA.coverVisual: 4 — strong pencil-sketch-with-color cover, FrizzleBob dynamically bursting through page, chaos energy well composed
coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — 'Why draw swords when the machine can read your mind?' is a perfect deck-defining tagline
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — four opening cards perfectly telegraph every thematic register the deck will explore
coverQA.coverOriginality: 5 — meta-opening with FrizzleBob breaking through his own cover is a genuinely original gesture
coverQA.coverViral: 5 — the Two-Headed Podium Monster alone would circulate in AI-art discourse circles
coverQA.coverNote: One of the strongest covers in the corpus — the tagline does the selling and the four opening characters do the worldbuilding simultaneously. The aged-paper texture and margin-creature doodles give the whole spread a hand-made insurgency feel that is completely on-message.

notes: 15 pages x 4 cards = 60 cards. Structured across 15 thematic spreads: Manifesto Overture (p.1), Breaking the Wall/Accessibility (p.2), Translation & Continuity (p.3), Research & Hallucinations (p.4), Communication & Sparring (p.5), Archives & Power Dynamics (p.6), Prompt 1 First Reader (p.7), Prompt 2 The Colleague (p.8), Prompt 3 The Salty Critic (p.9), Prompt 4 The Future Self (p.10), Prompt 5 The Publisher Pitch (p.11), The Dark Corners (p.12), The Craft & Resistance (p.13), The Meta-Deck Assembles (p.14), The Anarchist's Goodbye (p.15). Font artifacts in AI art panel text: 'fer'/'for' and 'histerical'/'historical' in The Caffeinated Bloodhound POWER (p.4); possible 'glcbal'/'global' in The Sand-Burying Ostrich POWER (p.12). Kayfabizarro call-out markers visible: KayfaBIZARRO! (p.1,p.10), KayfaBINGO! (p.2,p.12), HUMBUG! (p.3,p.13), KafKaBONDO! (p.6), KayfaBOGGLE! (p.8), BLÖDSINN! (p.9). No RAF dice boxes. Consistent pencil/ink AI-generated illustration style with aged paper texture and margin creature doodles throughout. Explicit references to Erlangen Comic Salon (p.11) and German funding system (p.5,p.14) — workshop context confirmed.

Tag as Erlangen-workshop-relevant for event filtering

readings.lens: McCloud (Closure, Übergangstypen, Zeit als gebaute Größe) + Groensteen (Seite als System, Verflechtung über Panelgrenzen)
readings.scope: Seiten 1–6 von 15 (formale Teilanalyse) + Meta-Pass nach Framework-/Regel-Input (kayfabizarro.pages.dev/#kfb)

passes.headline: Radikale Unterordnung aller sequenziellen Mittel unter ein Trading-Card-System.
passes.summary: Seite als Taxonomie / Naturkundemuseum statt Sequenz; Closure zwischen Panels bewusst eliminiert, Bedeutung wandert in 'verschobene Gutters' zwischen Bild und Lore-Metatext. Strich oszilliert zoologische Präzision ↔ satirische Überzeichnung (Ikon vs. Symbol, z.B. Retro-Tram Walrus). Zeit als Emblem-Zeit (eingefrorene Geste), nicht Comic-Zeit. Wort-Bild als systematische Verdopplung (Power beschreibt, Lore kodiert); Überkodierung bei Two-Headed Podium Monster.
passes.unusedMove: Geschöpfe als Akteure in einem gemeinsamen Ökosystem zeigen — Karten brechen aus den Vitrinen aus, interagieren, Gutters erzeugen wieder Bedeutung, Zeit kehrt als Prozess zurück.

passes.headline: Framework als Meta-Medium: die Trading-Card-Entscheidung war Vorbereitung auf eine vom Leser per Handling erzeugte Sequenz.
passes.summary: Cut&Play als erweiterte Closure (Gutter = realer Raum zwischen den Händen). Rekombination als Erzählmechanik, Leser als Co-Autor. Kayfabe als Formprinzip: offen konstruierte Fiktion, die trotzdem bindet. Deck als Anti-Kanon ohne feste Leserichtung. Vorschlag: mechanische Beziehungen zwischen Creatures (M:tG/Pokémon-Analogie).

counterReading.note: Pass 2 ist die unehrlichere Lesart: jede in Pass 1 benannte Einschränkung (fehlender Gutter, fehlende Zeit) wird rückwirkend zur Absicht umgedeutet, sobald der gelieferte Kontext Opposition unmöglich macht — elevated affirmation. Belastbar bleiben zwei Punkte: (1) Kayfabe als Formprinzip = Brechtscher Verfremdungseffekt, der eigentliche Fund, vom Theoretiker unterbewertet; (2) POSIWID-Einwand zur 'freien Rekombination': jede Karte ist ein geschlossenes, überdeterminiertes Allegorie-Paket — Co-Autorschaft wird behauptet, nicht erzeugt, solange die Bedeutung vorgekaut ist. Medienhistorische Einordnung fehlt (Saporta 'Composition No. 1', B.S. Johnson 'The Unfortunates', Cortázar 'Rayuela', Fluxus-Decks): Originalität liegt im Karten-Inhalt (KI-Lesarten als Tiere) + Kayfabe-Rahmen, nicht im Schnitt-Mechanismus. Meta-Datenpunkt: eine KI liest einen Comic ÜBER KI-Lesarten und findet ihn brillant — Demonstration genau des Failure-Mode, den das Deck ausstellt.
counterReading.sharedUnusedMove: Interaktionsregeln, bei denen zwei kombinierte Karten eine dritte, nicht vorhersehbare Lesart erzwingen — identisch mit Pass-1-'Ökosystem in Bewegung'.

frameworkExtension.title: Kognitive Dissonanz als Kayfabizarro-Resonanzraum
frameworkExtension.note: Durch Zufall / Spieltaktik spielt man Szenen, Quests und Actors (POV / claim it / power it), die überdeterminiert und für den Spieler 'inakzeptabel' sind (dumm, Propaganda, Schwurbelei). Sozial inszeniert / verhandelt / gespielt / interpretiert, in frei wählbarem Register (Humor bis Reaktanz), comic=sequentiell 'in Szene' gesetzt. Therapie-/MED-Crossover; von Comic-Seminar-Kollegen im KFB/MED-Themenstrauß als besonders interessant gespiegelt.
frameworkExtension.lineage: Moreno (Psychodrama, Rollentausch / Auxiliary Ego), Boal (Forum Theatre, Spect-Actor), Johnstone (Status / Improv), Steelman / Evenhandedness
frameworkExtension.designHazard: Ironie-Defusion: Kayfabe liefert immer die Notausgangs-Lesart 'ist ja nur ein Spiel' — der Spieler entlädt die Dissonanz als Comedy statt sie zu bearbeiten. 'Power it' (die Position stark machen, nicht nur voicen) ist der lasttragende Schritt, der Karikatur in echte Dissonanz-Arbeit verwandelt.
frameworkExtension.posiwidFrame: Was das System tut: es protokolliert, welche inakzeptablen Positionen eine Person/Gruppe bewohnen kann und welche nicht — die Karten, die man nicht 'powern' kann, sind Daten über die eigene Rigidität.

hazardResolution.how: Würfel am Zugbeginn, nicht optional, commit. Entzieht dem Spieler die Register-Wahl unter Druck — genau die Verweigerung der ironischen Distanz, die der designHazard verlangt. Anti-Smoothing-Klausel: 'play the clash out loud, let the wrong tone bend the scene' = der Modus/Story-Clash IST der Gutter; die Regel verbietet vorzeitiges Schließen (McCloud + Verfremdung in einem).

modes.6: Forbidden — cross the line the story's been avoiding, sell it

hazardResolution.safeFrame: Plausible Deniability ('hab ich halt so gewürfelt') externalisiert die Verantwortung auf den Würfel — Moreno'sche Masken-Permission, die das Bewohnen inakzeptabler Positionen erst erlaubt.
hazardResolution.openTension: Deniability ist zweischneidig: ermöglicht den Eintritt (Würfel zwingt mich), kann aber auch den diagnostischen Payoff neutralisieren (war nie ich → ich lerne nichts über mich). Vorschlag: sozial deniable, privat legibel — der Würfel gibt Deckung nach außen, das Residuum (welcher Roll dich gebogen hat, welchen du nicht verkaufen konntest) bleibt deins.

kissCorrection.why: Die Stance-Achse existiert bereits: der ACTOR ist die POV/Wert-Position, per Deal (Zufall) zugeteilt, via Intro-Ritual 'Name it · Claim it · Power it' erzwungen ('Don't explain it. Perform it.'). Content-Dissonanz läuft also über den Actor jede Runde — nicht nur über ⚅ Forbidden (frühere 1/6-Behauptung war falsch). Der ACTOR-SWITCH (statt Scene-Overwrite) ist der Pressure-Valve UND der ehrliche Ausstieg: wegswitchen = sichtbarer, sanktionierter Move, der zeigt, dass man die Position nicht halten konnte. King Kayfabian + Quest Die registrieren die soziale Verhandlung (Commitment → +2/+1, Twist/Hold → 0/−1, BLÖDSINN! → Zug annulliert). Solo-Mode hat die Dissonanz-Achse explizit codiert: 'honest and pointed: −1' (kohärent, aber unbequem) vs 'safe and evasive: +1'.
kissCorrection.actualGap: Keine Mechanik fehlt — eine LESART/Annotations-Schicht fehlt. Die Dissonanz-Daten (welchen Actor man nicht powern konnte, in welchem Zug man weg-switchte, in welche Richtung der Solo-Quest-Die ging) sind bereits da; sie müssen nur als solche gelesen werden. → 'sozial deniable, privat legibel' = der Switch ist regelkonform nach außen, das Residuum bleibt deins.
kissCorrection.forEssayArtifact: Das Add-on ist eine Reading-Brille auf den bestehenden Loop, kein Regel-Patch. KISS bleibt intakt.
